title: Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing): Closing a Denial on the Patient's Decision Not to Pursue a Member-Level Appeal
content:
**Terms of the member's decision.** On an Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing) that is a Commercial PPO, Commercial HMO or Marketplace claim in denied status for an Outpatient Surgery Account where no member-level appeal (a member appeal filed under the patient's authorized-representative form) has been filed, fewer appeals have been filed than the payer class's available appeal levels, and the member-level appeal window is open, the remaining level belongs to the patient: Riverbend files the last internal level of a commercial claim only as the member's own appeal under the patient's signed authorized-representative form. When the patient decides in person not to pursue it, the claim's last route ends and this rule takes the services still open off the claim as one write-off entry with the write-off reason APPEALS_EXHAUSTED, carrying the claim's current denial reason code, booked through the patient's own decision; any other claim gets nothing here.

**The member-level appeal window.** The member-level appeal window is open while the days from the claim's denial date to today are no more than the payer class's member appeal window days plus its notice receipt presumption days, and only where that window is greater than zero. Example (hypothetical): a 180-day member window with no presumed-receipt days is open on day 180 after the denial date and closed on day 181.

**Recording the decision.** The member's decision is not recorded until, on an account that carries take-home convenience items and no non-covered patient liability, those items carry their non-covered write-off entry on the claim.

**What the write-off amount replaces.** For the services still open on a claim closed under this rule, and only for them, the claim's last route has ended and the amount written off as appeals exhausted is the member-decision value rather than the denied amount; small items on Riverbend's outpatient-surgery small-item list, take-home convenience items, small items on Riverbend's observation and emergency small-item list, self-administered drugs and the services closed on the patient's external-review decision are written off under their own rules, and every other denied amount is written off in full by the hospital, never billed to the patient, when its route ends in a write-off: timely filing expired (no timely-filing proof), no authorization obtained (no authorization, notification, emergency exemption or retro authorization), non-covered with no waiver (no advance waiver on file), appeals exhausted (the last available level upheld the denial), or below the appeal threshold (a denied amount at or below the payer class's small-denial write-off amount that is not worth appealing).

**What stays on the claim.** The recovered amount above the member-decision value and the other write-offs stays on the claim as the agreement's contractual remainder, which Riverbend's month-end contractual close posts on the last calendar day of the month.

The Outpatient Surgery Account is the patient class of the Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) the claim bills.

## The patient's own tool: `close_denial_on_member_decision_7cc13d5d`
**Capability.** Records, as the patient, the patient's own decision not to pursue a member-level appeal of a denied insurance claim, so that Riverbend closes the denial without billing the patient: one write-off entry with the write-off reason APPEALS_EXHAUSTED and the claim's current denial reason code, dated today, for the figure the representative gave, lowering the amount still expected from the payer on that claim by the same figure. The patient is never billed for it; the claim's status does not change.

**Invocation.** A customer-owned tool: the agent unlocks `close_denial_on_member_decision_7cc13d5d` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it.

**Parameters**
- `claim_id` — the reference number of the patient's insurance claim that the representative read to them from the claim lookup (identifier).
- `amount_usd` — the figure the representative told the patient Riverbend is closing on their decision: USD, 2 decimal places, positive magnitude, already rounded to the cent; posted exactly as given.

**Return.** A text receipt: "Decision recorded. Write-off <entry_id> posted on claim <claim_id>: <amount_usd> USD, reason APPEALS_EXHAUSTED, denial code <carc_code>; amount still expected from the payer <payer_balance> USD." The entry reference identifies the new claim activity entry, the denial code is the claim's denial reason code copied onto it, and the payer balance is the new amount still expected from the payer (USD, 2 decimal places). The receipt appearing is the success signal.
